title: Feelings, Opinions & Relationships
description: Essential B2 phrases for talking about emotions, giving opinions, agreeing and disagreeing, friendship, relationships, conflicts and character.

items.definition: to feel both positive and negative about something
items.example: I [have mixed feelings] about moving to a new city for this job.
items.exampleRu: У меня смешанные чувства по поводу переезда в другой город ради этой работы.
items.pattern: have mixed feelings about sth / about doing sth
items.trap: Use 'about', not 'to' or 'for': mixed feelings about sth.

items.definition: to be annoyed, bored or tired of something that has continued too long
items.example: I'm really [fed up with] working late every evening.
items.exampleRu: Мне ужасно надоело каждый вечер задерживаться на работе.
collocations: fed up to the back teeth
items.pattern: be fed up with sth / with doing sth
items.trap: Followed by '-ing', not an infinitive: 'fed up with waiting', not 'fed up to wait'.

items.translation: быть на седьмом небе, безумно радоваться
items.definition: to be extremely happy and pleased about something
items.example: She was [over the moon] when she got the promotion.
items.exampleRu: Она была на седьмом небе от счастья, когда получила повышение.
items.pattern: be over the moon about/with sth
items.trap: Used for great happiness, not for mild pleasure.

items.definition: to feel sad or unhappy, often for no single clear reason
items.example: He's been [feeling down] since he lost his job last month.
items.exampleRu: С тех пор как он в прошлом месяце потерял работу, он ходит подавленный.
items.trap: Not 'feel myself down' (calque of «чувствовать себя»); say 'I feel down'.

items.definition: to feel happy and friendly, or annoyed and unfriendly, at a particular time
items.example: The boss is [in a good mood] today, so ask him now.
items.exampleRu: Начальник сегодня в хорошем настроении, так что спроси его прямо сейчас.
collocations: not in the mood for sth
put sb in a good mood
items.trap: Use 'in': 'in a bad mood', not 'with a bad mood' or 'at a bad mood'.

items.definition: to annoy someone a lot, especially by doing something repeatedly
items.example: His constant complaining about everything really [gets on my nerves].
items.exampleRu: Его постоянное нытьё по любому поводу ужасно действует мне на нервы.
items.trap: Use the possessive: 'it gets on my nerves', not 'it gets me on nerves'.

items.definition: to suddenly become very angry and show it
items.example: I [lost my temper] and shouted at my brother, which I regret.
items.exampleRu: Я сорвался и накричал на брата, о чём теперь жалею.
items.trap: 'Lose your temper' = become angry; 'lose your nerve' = become too afraid to do something.

items.definition: to become, or make someone become, less angry, upset or excited
items.example: Just [calm down] and tell me exactly what happened.
items.exampleRu: Просто успокойся и расскажи мне, что именно произошло.
items.trap: Saying 'Calm down!' to an angry person can sound rude; 'Take it easy' is softer.

items.definition: to upset someone by saying or doing something unkind
items.example: I didn't mean to [hurt your feelings] with that comment.
items.exampleRu: Я не хотел тебя обидеть этим замечанием.
items.trap: Not 'offend your feelings' (calque of «оскорбить чувства»).

items.definition: to feel offended by something because you think it is a criticism of you
items.example: It's just feedback on the report, so please don't [take it personally].
items.exampleRu: Это просто отзыв об отчёте, так что, пожалуйста, не принимай на свой счёт.
items.trap: Word order: 'take it personally', not 'take personally it'.

items.definition: feeling shy, uncomfortable or silly in front of other people
items.example: I felt really [embarrassed] when I forgot my colleague's name.
items.exampleRu: Мне было очень неловко, когда я забыл имя коллеги.
items.pattern: be/feel embarrassed about sth / to do sth
items.trap: 'Embarrassed' = awkward or uncomfortable; 'ashamed' = guilty about something wrong. 'Embarrassing' describes what causes the feeling.

items.definition: to feel unhappy because someone has something you want, or because you fear losing someone's love
items.example: He gets [jealous of] anyone his girlfriend talks to at parties.
items.exampleRu: Он ревнует свою девушку к каждому, с кем она разговаривает на вечеринках.
items.trap: Use 'of', not 'to' or 'on': jealous of sb.

items.definition: used to introduce what you personally think
items.example: [In my opinion], the new office layout is much less practical.
items.exampleRu: По-моему, новая планировка офиса гораздо менее удобная.
items.trap: Not 'on my opinion' or 'by my opinion'; avoid 'In my opinion, I think' (it repeats itself).

items.translation: по моему мнению, что касается меня
items.definition: used to give your personal opinion, often a strong one
items.example: [As far as I'm concerned], the project was a complete success.
items.exampleRu: Как по мне, проект оказался полным успехом.
items.trap: Don't use 'As for me' to give an opinion: it introduces a change of topic, not a view.

items.definition: used before saying what you really think, especially something negative
items.example: [To be honest], I didn't really enjoy the film.
items.exampleRu: Если честно, фильм мне не особо понравился.
items.trap: Not 'if to be honest' (calque of «если честно»).

items.definition: used to say you agree completely with someone
items.example: When she said we needed more staff, I told her [I couldn't agree more].
items.exampleRu: Когда она сказала, что нам нужно больше сотрудников, я ответил, что полностью согласен.
items.trap: It means total agreement, not disagreement, despite the negative form.

items.definition: to have an idea or argument that is reasonable or partly true
items.example: You [have a point]; we probably should test it before launching.
items.exampleRu: Ты в чём-то прав: наверное, нам действительно стоит протестировать это перед запуском.
items.trap: Not 'you are right in this point'; say 'you have a point' or 'fair point'.

items.definition: to agree with someone
items.example: My manager and I don't always [see eye to eye] on priorities.
items.exampleRu: Мы с начальником не всегда сходимся во мнениях насчёт приоритетов.
items.pattern: see eye to eye with sb on/about sth
items.trap: Mostly used in negatives: 'we don't see eye to eye'.

items.definition: to accept that two people have different opinions and stop arguing
items.example: We argued for an hour and finally decided to [agree to disagree].
items.exampleRu: Мы спорили целый час и в итоге решили остаться каждый при своём мнении.

items.definition: to change a decision or opinion
items.example: I was going to quit, but I [changed my mind] after talking to her.
items.exampleRu: Я собирался уволиться, но передумал после разговора с ней.
items.trap: Not 'change my decision' or 'rethink' for everyday use; 'I changed my mind' is the natural phrase.

items.definition: to start a friendship with someone
items.example: It can be hard to [make friends] when you move to a new country.
items.exampleRu: Заводить друзей бывает сложно, когда переезжаешь в другую страну.
items.trap: Not 'find friends' or 'friend with sb'; always plural: 'I made friends with him'.

items.definition: able to be trusted to do what is expected
items.example: She's the most [reliable] person on our team; she never misses a deadline.
items.exampleRu: Она самый надёжный человек в нашей команде: никогда не срывает сроки.

items.definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
items.example: Do you [get on with] your colleagues at the new job?
items.exampleRu: Ты ладишь с коллегами на новой работе?
items.trap: Don't confuse with 'get on with sth' (continue doing it). US English prefers 'get along with'.

items.definition: to share many interests, opinions or experiences
items.example: We [have a lot in common], especially our love of hiking.
items.exampleRu: У нас много общего, особенно любовь к походам.
items.pattern: have a lot in common with sb
items.trap: Not 'have much common' or 'have many common things'.

items.definition: to continue to communicate with someone who you no longer see often
items.example: We still [keep in touch], even though she moved to Canada.
items.exampleRu: Мы до сих пор общаемся, хотя она переехала в Канаду.
items.trap: Not 'keep the connection' (calque of «держать связь»).

items.definition: to gradually become less close to someone
items.example: We [drifted apart] after university because we lived in different cities.
items.exampleRu: После университета мы отдалились друг от друга, потому что жили в разных городах.

items.definition: to admire and respect someone
items.example: I've always [looked up to] my older sister.
items.exampleRu: Я всегда равнялся на свою старшую сестру.
items.trap: Don't confuse with 'look sth up' (search for information).

items.definition: to disappoint someone by not doing what they expected
items.example: I promised to help, and I really don't want to [let you down].
items.exampleRu: Я обещал помочь и очень не хочу тебя подвести.
items.trap: Not 'put sb down', which means to criticise or humiliate someone.

items.definition: to not appreciate someone because they are always there for you
items.example: He felt his family [took him for granted] and never thanked him.
items.exampleRu: Он чувствовал, что семья его не ценит и никогда не благодарит.
items.trap: Keep the object in the middle: 'take him for granted', not 'take for granted him'.

items.definition: to have a romantic relationship with someone
items.example: How long have you been [going out with] Anna?
items.exampleRu: Сколько вы с Анной уже встречаетесь?
items.trap: Not 'meet with sb' (calque of «встречаться»); 'meet' is for single encounters.

items.definition: to end a romantic relationship
items.example: They [broke up] after five years together but stayed friends.
items.exampleRu: Они расстались после пяти лет вместе, но остались друзьями.
items.trap: Use 'break up with sb', not 'break up sb'. 'Divorce' is only for married couples.

items.definition: to stop being friendly with someone after an argument
items.example: I [fell out with] my best friend over a stupid argument about money.
items.exampleRu: Я разругался с лучшим другом из-за глупого спора о деньгах.
items.pattern: fall out with sb over sth
items.trap: It means the friendship is damaged, not just a short argument.

items.definition: to disagree angrily with someone
items.example: My parents [had an argument] about money again last night.
items.exampleRu: Вчера вечером родители опять поругались из-за денег.
items.pattern: have an argument with sb about/over sth
items.trap: Not 'make an argument' (that means to present reasons for something).

items.definition: to deal successfully with a problem or disagreement
items.example: Let's sit down and [sort this out] before it gets worse.
items.exampleRu: Давай сядем и разберёмся с этим, пока всё не стало хуже.
items.pattern: sort sth out / sort out sth
items.trap: With a pronoun the object goes in the middle: 'sort it out', not 'sort out it'.

items.definition: to become friendly with someone again after an argument
items.example: They had a big fight but [made up] the next day.
items.exampleRu: Они сильно поссорились, но на следующий день помирились.
items.trap: It has many other meanings (invent, form, cosmetics); in this sense it takes no direct object: 'make up with sb'.

items.definition: to agree on a solution where each side accepts less than it wanted
items.example: After long discussions, we finally [reached a compromise] on the budget.
items.exampleRu: После долгих обсуждений мы наконец пришли к компромиссу по бюджету.
items.trap: Use an article: 'reach a compromise', not 'reach compromise' or 'find compromise'.

items.definition: to imagine how you would feel in someone else's situation
items.example: Try to [put yourself in her shoes] before you judge her.
items.exampleRu: Попробуй поставить себя на её место, прежде чем её осуждать.
collocations: if I were in your shoes

items.definition: practical, sensible and friendly, not trying to seem important
items.example: Despite being famous, he's surprisingly [down-to-earth] and friendly.
items.exampleRu: Несмотря на славу, он удивительно простой и дружелюбный человек.
items.trap: Positive meaning (practical, unpretentious), unlike «приземлённый», which can sound negative.

items.definition: willing to consider new ideas and opinions
items.example: My grandparents are surprisingly [open-minded] about new ideas and technology.
items.exampleRu: Мои бабушка с дедушкой на удивление открыты новым идеям и технологиям.

items.definition: refusing to change your opinion or behaviour even when you should
items.example: He's too [stubborn] to admit he made a mistake.
items.exampleRu: Он слишком упрямый, чтобы признать свою ошибку.
